questions.text: Which defect is most influenced by atmospheric pollution?
questions.expl: Airborne pollutants (acidic gases, particulates) chemically attack and erode building surfaces over time.

questions.text: Which defect is mainly due to excessive water–cement ratio in concrete?
questions.expl: Excess water increases porosity and drying shrinkage, leading to greater shrinkage cracking and reduced durability/strength.

questions.text: Which condition primarily governs the severity of corrosion-related defects in RCC?
questions.expl: The severity of reinforcement corrosion is governed mainly by the exposure environment (chloride presence, humidity, carbonation exposure).

questions.text: Which crack repair diagnosis is associated with active corrosion rather than past corrosion in RCC?
options: Cracks parallel to reinforcement with dampness
questions.expl: Fresh cracks along reinforcement combined with visible dampness indicate ongoing (active), not merely historic, corrosion activity.

questions.text: Which defect suggests poor workmanship during concreting rather than a design deficiency?
questions.expl: Honeycombing results from poor placement/compaction practices during concreting — a workmanship issue rather than a design flaw.

questions.text: Which sign confirms carbonation-induced corrosion in RCC primarily occurs due to:
questions.expl: Carbonation lowers the concrete's alkalinity (pH), destroying the passive film that normally protects embedded steel, thereby triggering corrosion.

questions.text: Which defect in RCC roofs directly indicates failure of expansion joints?
options: Cracks along joint line with leakage
questions.expl: Failed expansion joints show characteristic cracking and water leakage precisely along the joint line.

questions.text: Which defect suggests failure of roof slope design?
questions.expl: Inadequate roof slope causes standing water (ponding), leading to visible seepage marks and eventual leakage.

questions.text: The primary objective of surface preparation before concrete repair is to:
options: Ensure proper bond between old and new material
questions.expl: Surface preparation is done chiefly to achieve a sound, clean substrate that ensures good bonding between the existing concrete and new repair material.

questions.text: Which method of surface preparation uses compressed air or water at high pressure?
questions.expl: Sand blasting propels abrasive particles using compressed air (or water) at high pressure to clean/roughen a surface.

questions.text: Which repair material is most suitable for filling fine non-structural cracks in concrete?
questions.expl: Low-viscosity epoxy resin can penetrate and effectively fill very fine (non-structural) cracks.

questions.text: Routing and sealing of cracks is generally adopted for:
questions.expl: Routing and sealing (V-grooving and filling with sealant) is a simple technique suited to fine, non-structural (e.g. shrinkage) cracks.

questions.text: Which material is commonly used as a bonding agent between old concrete and repair mortar?
questions.expl: Epoxy bonding compounds provide a strong, reliable adhesive interface between old and new concrete/mortar in repair work.

questions.text: Which technique is most suitable for repairing honeycombed concrete areas?
options: Removal and replacement with repair mortar
questions.expl: Severely honeycombed concrete requires removal of the defective material and replacement with sound repair mortar/concrete.

questions.text: Shotcreting is primarily used in repair works to:
options: Restore and strengthen damaged concrete sections
questions.expl: Shotcrete (sprayed concrete/mortar) is used to restore lost section and strengthen damaged or deteriorated concrete members.

questions.text: Which property of polymer-modified mortar makes it suitable for repair works?
questions.expl: Polymer modification enhances bond strength, flexibility and reduces permeability, making such mortars well suited to repair applications.

questions.text: Which crack repair method involves injecting material under pressure?
questions.expl: Injection grouting forces (often epoxy) grout under pressure into cracks to restore monolithic integrity.

questions.text: Which material is most commonly used for grouting fine cracks in RCC structures?
questions.expl: Epoxy grout, with its very low viscosity and high strength/adhesion, is preferred for injecting fine cracks in RCC.

questions.text: Which method of crack repair involves inserting steel bars across cracks?
questions.expl: Stitching uses steel staples/bars drilled and grouted across a crack to mechanically tie the two sides together.

questions.text: The main disadvantage of cement mortar repair in thin sections is:
questions.expl: Cement mortar applied in thin repair layers is prone to drying shrinkage cracking due to the high surface-to-volume ratio.

questions.text: Which surface preparation technique is most effective for removing oil and grease from concrete?
questions.expl: Acid etching (or degreasing agents) is effective at breaking down and removing oil/grease contamination that mechanical methods alone cannot fully remove.

questions.text: Which repair technique is preferred for extensive shallow surface defects in concrete slabs?
questions.expl: Overlaying (applying a new topping/repair layer) is well suited to widespread shallow surface defects across a slab.

questions.text: Which property of repair material is most critical for overhead repairs?
questions.expl: For overhead (soffit) repairs, the material must not sag or fall off before setting — non-sag (thixotropic) behaviour is critical.

questions.text: Which method of surface preparation creates a roughened profile without damaging sound concrete?
questions.expl: Light sand blasting roughens the surface texture sufficiently for bonding, without damaging the underlying sound concrete.

questions.text: Which repair material is most suitable where rapid strength gain is required?
questions.expl: Rapid-hardening, cement-based proprietary repair mortars are specifically formulated for fast strength gain in urgent repair situations.

questions.text: Which defect repair requires removal of corroded reinforcement (rust) before application of repair mortar?
questions.expl: Repairing corrosion-induced spalling requires cleaning rust off (and sometimes replacing) the corroded reinforcement before applying new repair mortar.

questions.text: Which surface preparation step is essential before applying epoxy bonding agents?
questions.expl: Epoxy bonding agents require a dry, clean, laitance-free surface for effective adhesion, unlike cementitious bonding agents that may need a damp surface.

questions.text: Which factor most influences selection of crack repair method?
questions.expl: The choice of repair method depends primarily on whether the crack is active (still moving) or dormant, and on its width.

questions.text: The most critical first step in repairing corrosion-affected RCC members is to:
options: Remove loose concrete and expose reinforcement
questions.expl: All loose, delaminated concrete must first be removed to expose the corroded reinforcement fully before any treatment or repair can proceed.

questions.text: After cleaning corroded reinforcement, which treatment is applied to protect steel before repair?
questions.expl: A specialized anti-corrosion protective coating (e.g. zinc-rich or polymer-modified cementitious coating) is applied to cleaned steel before patching.

questions.text: Which method is most suitable for restoring load-carrying capacity of severely corroded RCC columns?
questions.expl: Column jacketing (adding a reinforced concrete or steel jacket) is used to restore/enhance load capacity of severely deteriorated columns.

questions.text: Which method is commonly adopted for repairing a failed damp-proof course in existing buildings?
questions.expl: Chemical (silicone/siloxane) injection into the wall creates a new water-repellent barrier where an existing DPC has failed.

questions.text: Rising dampness is effectively controlled by providing DPC at:
questions.expl: The damp-proof course is provided at plinth level, just above ground, to intercept capillary rise of moisture into the walls.

questions.text: Which material is most commonly used for flexible DPC in modern construction?
questions.expl: Bituminous felt is a common flexible damp-proof course material, able to accommodate minor movement while remaining impervious.

questions.text: Which waterproofing system is most suitable for flat RCC roofs?
questions.expl: Mud phuska (a lime-mud-brick jelly treatment) is a traditional but effective waterproofing/insulation system historically used on flat RCC roofs (modern practice also uses membrane systems).

questions.text: Failure of waterproofing in bathrooms usually leads to:
questions.expl: Leaking bathroom waterproofing typically causes dampness to migrate into adjoining walls and ceilings below.

questions.text: Which test is commonly used to check leakage in bathrooms after waterproofing treatment?
questions.expl: A ponding test — flooding the surface with water and observing over 24–48 hours — checks for leaks after waterproofing.

questions.text: Expansion joints in buildings are primarily provided to:
questions.expl: Expansion joints allow buildings to accommodate thermal expansion/contraction (and sometimes shrinkage movement) without inducing cracking.

questions.text: Failure of sealant in expansion joints generally results in:
questions.expl: A failed joint sealant allows water to penetrate the joint, leading to leakage and associated cracking/corrosion issues.

questions.text: Which sealant property is most important for joints subjected to movement?
questions.expl: Movement joints require a sealant with high elasticity so it can stretch and compress repeatedly without losing its seal.

questions.text: Which repair measure is most effective for recurring roof leakage due to cracks?
options: Filling cracks with cement mortar only
questions.expl: A continuous waterproof membrane bridges cracks and provides durable, effective long-term protection against recurring roof leakage.

questions.text: Which repair material is commonly used for sealing construction joints in water-retaining structures?
questions.expl: Water stop sealants (PVC/rubber water stops or specialized joint sealants) are specifically designed to seal joints in water-retaining structures.

questions.text: Corrosion repair in marine environments requires special attention due to the presence of:
questions.expl: Marine environments have high chloride concentrations, which aggressively depassivate steel and accelerate reinforcement corrosion.

questions.text: The most effective long-term strategy to minimize repair frequency in buildings is:
questions.expl: A systematic, planned preventive maintenance programme minimizes the frequency and cost of future repairs over the building's life.

questions.text: The most important reason for conducting maintenance audits of buildings is to:
questions.expl: Maintenance audits are conducted primarily to systematically assess a building's structural health and serviceability.

questions.text: Which defect indicates loss of bond between plaster and masonry due to moisture action?
questions.expl: Moisture trapped behind plaster causes it to lose adhesion, resulting in peeling and bulging.

questions.text: Which investigation method is most suitable for determining depth of corrosion in RCC?
questions.expl: Half-cell potential mapping is used to assess the probability and extent (spatially) of active corrosion in reinforcement.

questions.text: Which defect in concrete floors is primarily due to excessive surface finishing and trowelling?
questions.expl: Over-trowelling seals the surface prematurely, trapping bleed water/air beneath and causing blisters to form.

questions.text: Which crack pattern is most critical from a structural safety point of view?
questions.expl: Progressively widening flexural cracks signal ongoing structural distress and are the most safety-critical among the listed options.

questions.text: Which factor primarily controls the effectiveness of chemical DPC injection?
questions.expl: The porosity of the masonry governs how effectively the injected chemical DPC solution can spread and form a continuous water-repellent barrier.

questions.text: Which waterproofing failure is commonly caused by inadequate curing of the treatment layer?
questions.expl: Insufficiently cured waterproofing treatments are prone to premature shrinkage cracking and loss of bond (debonding) from the substrate.

questions.text: Which repair method is most suitable for sealing leaking construction joints in basements?
questions.expl: Polyurethane injection expands and seals actively leaking joints even under water pressure, making it well suited to basement joint leaks.

questions.text: Which maintenance strategy minimizes life-cycle cost of buildings most effectively?
questions.expl: Preventive maintenance, by addressing issues early, has been shown to minimize total life-cycle costs compared to reactive strategies.

questions.text: Which material property is most important for repair mortars used in wet areas?
questions.expl: For repairs in wet/damp-prone areas, low water absorption (impermeability) is critical to prevent recurring moisture-related failure.

questions.text: Which defect is a clear indication of failure of roof slope design?
questions.expl: Standing water (ponding) and consequent seepage stains reveal that the roof slope/drainage design is inadequate.

questions.text: Which repair approach is most appropriate when cracks are still actively moving?
questions.expl: Active (still-moving) cracks need a flexible sealant that can accommodate ongoing movement, rather than rigid materials that would re-crack.

questions.text: Which defect in masonry walls usually indicates absence of DPC?
options: Damp patches with salt deposits near floor
questions.expl: Persistent dampness and salt staining near floor level are classic signs that no effective damp-proof course exists at plinth level.

questions.text: Which factor most accelerates deterioration of buildings in coastal areas?
questions.expl: The chloride-laden atmosphere near coasts aggressively promotes reinforcement corrosion, accelerating structural deterioration.

questions.text: Which waterproofing method provides both thermal insulation and water resistance on roofs?
questions.expl: Brick bat coba (broken brick bats set in lime/cement mortar) provides both thermal insulation and a waterproofing layer on flat roofs.

questions.text: Which joint is specifically provided to accommodate differential settlement between two structures?
questions.expl: A settlement joint is specifically designed to allow independent movement between adjacent structures subject to differential settlement.

questions.text: The most reliable way to ensure durability of repair works is to:
questions.expl: Repairs will only last if the underlying root cause of deterioration (e.g. moisture ingress, ongoing corrosion) is first eliminated.

questions.text: Which joint is provided between two adjacent buildings to allow independent movement?
questions.expl: Expansion joints between adjacent buildings/blocks allow each to move independently under thermal and other effects.

questions.text: Which repair material is commonly used for sealing construction joints in water-retaining structures (repeated)?
questions.expl: Water stop sealants remain the standard choice for joints in tanks and other water-retaining structures.
